headline: Preprint derives sharp force-space density thresholds for forced Navier–Stokes breakdown
summary: Cao, Chi, and Nie report sharp thresholds for how close smooth forcing can be, in weak Sobolev norms, while producing classical breakdown by a prescribed time. For fixed positive viscosity and zero initial velocity, their preprint claims density exactly below s=1/2 in relative L1_t H^s_x on both T3 and R3; on R3 it gives the corresponding L2_t H^s_x threshold s<-1/2. The construction glues in a compact forced blowup block attributed to OpenAI while changing the external force. These are preprint claims not independently reproduced here, and they do not address the unforced Millennium problem or independently verify the building block.
